comment: I took GEOG210 & Ecotourism. She was overall a great professor! Work load was quite a lot (I did read every assignment posted & put full effort into each discussion/essay). I couldn't have done it alongside an internship with the level of workload like most in the summer. Overall it was a pretty cool course, just get ready to read and write a ton.

I learned so much & enjoyed the class but the lectures were sometimes disorganized b/c she had so many different things she wanted to show us for a single concept. It was hard to follow along with what we were learning at times b/c she jumped around a lot. Very attainable A, you can do well without working super hard. Very lenient with deadlines

she's low key crazy; passionate about the environment but in ways that are not helpful in the classroom. lots of reading that is not used in class time and i dont even know what to tell you about the subject

Dr Finley-Brook is very passionate about environmental justice. Her teaching style tends to expect the same passion from her students - which is unrealstic given the balancing act of being a college student. This class culminates in a large research project which is, in my view, excessively long (10-15 pages). Readings and lectures are interesting.

MFB is such a great professor. I wish I had taken a class with her earlier in my college career. She is so passionate about her material and really knows her stuff. She had us work on a big geopolitical project the whole semester. As long as you choose sth you're really into, you're gonna learn a lot and enjoy the class. The readings are manageable

She is extremely unorganized, which means that you will go weeks without work to three huge assignments due within a few days of each other at the end of the semester. She focuses the class on what she wants to talk about and other opinions are ignored. She is very passionate about the environment, but not a good teacher for college and this course

She is extremely passionate about her subject and wants you to be as well. If you have a future in ecotourism, environmental protection, that type of thing, then by all means. Other than that, no reason you should want to be in this course. She pushes her agenda on students forcing them to help her own pet projects. At times, she seems unhinged.

By far my favorite professor at U of R. She is so brilliant and she explains things incredibly well. She's clear with her instructions and expectations and as long as you actually listen, pay attention, think, and do the readings, her courses aren't hard. I've taken two classes with Dr. Finley-Brook (GEOG210 & 370) & I have no complaints at all.

She is a great teacher because she is so passionate about the subject. The class material is interesting and relevant, as are the essay prompts. Some of the readings can be boring. The exams are take home, open note essay questions. She covers a lot of material in class but posts all the powerpoints online. She is inspiring and passionate.

Her projects and assignments were very unclear. The only chance to get clarity is during office hours and she may try to help you. She was snobbish if you did not have the same knowledge as she had in the subject. I started this year as a geography major but now I want nothing to do with the subject. Do not talk the class if you don't have to!!!

The material was interesting but Professor Finley-Brook is horrible. She is condescending, rather rude, and thinks everyone should know as much as she does. Her (very high) expectations of assignments are unclear and she expects a lot of participation. Do not take her unless you want to be very stressed out.

I highly discourage anyone from taking her class. She is very unclear with what she wants, and if you want a good grade you will have to go to office hours often. Class is boring and she assigns a lot of reading. I highly discourage you taking her class, if it is not necessary.

Literally the worst professor I have ever had at the University of Richmond. She is so unclear, I had no idea when an assignment was do, and she jumbled the class together. Please, do not take her. For the sake of your sanity and stress levels. The class is not hard, it's just so unorganized. I do not know why she has such a high rating.

The class felt like it was thrown together. Towards the end of the semester, we were doing three serious projects at once. No one knew what was going on. She complains about being busy all the time so she expects you to know everything. Her assignments are very unspecific and when you turn something in, you do not know if you did the right thing.

Perhaps the best geography and environmental studies professor. I've taken several classes with her and have always learned a lot each time. Her classes have a great balance of lecture, reading and peer collaboration. She's very passionate about the material and is a fair grader.

I had her for Green Schools. I thought she did a great job presenting the topic in an interesting way. Most of my class didn't like her but she was always helpful and the readings were nothing compared to how much other FYS's had to do. She is a hard grader but she is also fair.

Green schools is a great FYS for those interested in environmental issues. And for those who aren't,  Finley-Brook is very passionate about the area and will get you to like it! She is very knowledgeable about the topics. The clas has a moderate amount of reading but it overall not very hard. She is a great professor but talks a lot and very loudly

Finley-Brook is an awesome teacher. She's really passionate about the topics she teachers, and sometimes it seems like she's a little forceful during in-class engagements. She expects a lot of participation and collaboration. You think the class is easy until you take her quizzes. Make sure you study and do the readings beforehand.
